title: Price a box of twelve pastries

messages.text: A box of twelve pastries costs me $14.20 to make. What should I charge to keep a 60% margin? And what happens if I give regulars 10% off?

## Charge $35.50 for the box

A 60% margin means the cost is the other 40% of the price: $14.20 / 0.40.

| | Price | You keep | Margin |
|---|---|---|---|
| Full price | $35.50 | $21.30 | 60% |
| Regulars, 10% off | $31.95 | $17.75 | 56% |

The discount costs four points of margin on every box a regular buys. Two ways to live with it:

1. Keep $35.50 and accept 56% from regulars. If they are one buyer in four, the average is still 59%.
2. List the box at **$39.45**, so the price after the discount is the $35.50 you wanted.

```
price  = cost / (1 - margin)        14.20 / 0.40 = 35.50
listed = price / (1 - discount)     35.50 / 0.90 = 39.45
```
